claims.claim: The entire Mastercard Developers reference can be read logged out: every documentation URL serves a plain-markdown twin at /index.md, and a 527 KB llms.txt indexes 94 documented services.
claims.quote: You can access all of our documentation as plain text markdown files by adding `/index.md` to the end of any documentation url.
claims.title: Working with llms.txt
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: The HTML site is a JavaScript SPA (empty shell to curl and WebFetch); the .md twins and llms.txt are static and were fetched with curl with no login. 30 platform docs and 15 product docs were read this way. llms.txt contains 94 'serviceId:' entries and 74 entries under '## Products'.

claims.claim: Sandbox credentials are self-service: sign up, create a project, select APIs, generate and download credentials, and test in Sandbox with no approval step for most APIs.
claims.quote: Click the “Open Project” button. Now you’re ready to test in Sandbox.
claims.title: Quick Start Guide | Platform Overview | Mastercard Developers
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Rendered in a browser tab logged out; the same page is also served as quick-start-guide/index.md (7,105 bytes, fetched by curl). Steps: create/activate account, create project, select APIs, 'Generate and download your credentials', open project. Team Management doc adds: 'A project can have a maximum of 10 admin members and a maximum of 20 members in total.'

claims.claim: Not every sandbox is open: some services put a new project's Sandbox access into an 'Under Review' state pending the service team's approval, and private services are hidden from the API picker until access is requested.
claims.quote: Some services require approval before granting access to their Sandbox environment.
claims.title: Quick Start Guide | Platform Overview | Mastercard Developers
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Same FAQ also says: 'A service may not appear in the APIs dropdown if it’s private and you don’t have access to it.' A forum post of 2026-08-31 shows a Confirmed Fraud (FLD) project stuck at 'SANDBOX Pending'.

claims.claim: Portal-issued keys expire after 13 months; the portal emails expiry reminders, although the two docs disagree on the reminder schedule.
claims.quote: Keys generated on Mastercard Developers are valid for 13 months.
claims.title: Quick Start Guide | Platform Overview | Mastercard Developers
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Quick Start says reminders at '60, 30, 15, 5, and 1 day'; the OAuth Keys guide says '90, 60, 30, 15, 7, and 1 day(s)'. See contradictions.

claims.claim: Production credentials are minted instantly at request time but stay inactive until Mastercard approves the production request; prerequisites are company verification, 'commercial countries' and a Business Relationship Type that covers the API.
claims.quote: Production credentials are generated instantaneously but they are only activated once your Production request is approved.
claims.title: Quick Start Guide | Platform Overview | Mastercard Developers
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: BRT doc (account-management/business-relationship-type/index.md): 'To request Production access, the API services added to your project must align with the BRT assigned to your company.' Missing BRTs are added via an emailed 'Customer Onboarding Platform' questionnaire; 'It may take up to 2 hours' to reflect. SSO customers skip company verification.

claims.claim: Company verification on the developer portal is keyed to the Mastercard Company ID (CID) and pre-populates from the company's Mastercard Connect account, tying the developer portal to the gated client portal.
claims.quote: If a corresponding Mastercard Connect account is found, the company data will be pre-populated.
claims.title: Company Verification
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: CID is 'a 6-10 digit ID that Mastercard assigns to a business'. Verified accounts show a VERIFIED badge on My Account. Non-Connect customers enter company details and a request goes for manual review ('VERIFICATION IN PROGRESS').

claims.claim: OAuth 1.0a with RSA-SHA256 request signing is the default authentication scheme across the portal; OAuth 2.0 (FAPI 2.0) and mutual TLS are the two alternatives.
claims.quote: This is the default authentication mechanism used by most APIs on Mastercard Developers.
claims.title: Authentication
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Page lists three protocols: OAuth 1.0a, OAuth 2.0 ('client credentials flow' plus FAPI 2.0), Mutual TLS (mTLS). No plain API-key scheme is offered.

claims.claim: OAuth 1.0a mechanics: a 97-character non-secret consumer key plus a 2048-bit RSA private signing key (RSA only), signature method fixed to RSA-SHA256 with the oauth_body_hash extension; the portal can generate the key pair in the browser so Mastercard never holds the private key.
claims.quote: Consumer keys are 97-character identifiers for client applications consuming Mastercard APIs.
claims.title: Using OAuth 1.0a to Access Mastercard APIs
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: 'The signing key is a 2048-bit private RSA key'; 'It must be RSA-SHA256'. CSR doc: 'For OAuth 1.0a, only RSA keys are supported'. OAuth Keys guide: 'When you choose this option, your browser generates the private key and downloads it for you. Mastercard never sees your private key.' Keys are delivered as PKCS#12 (.p12).

claims.claim: Mastercard's OAuth 2.0 is the FAPI 2.0 Security Profile: client authentication by private_key_jwt and sender-constrained access tokens via DPoP (ES256 or PS256), with a DPoP-Nonce handshake; sandbox token endpoint is sandbox.api.mastercard.com/oauth/token and example tokens live 900 seconds.
claims.quote: Mastercard implements the "FAPI2SP private key + DPoP" approach, which creates 2 layers of protection:
claims.title: Using OAuth 2.0 to Access Mastercard APIs
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Guide shows htu 'https://sandbox.api.mastercard.com/oauth/token' and a token response with '"expires_in": 900'. Only the sandbox token endpoint is printed; no production token URL found. OAuth Keys guide: 'For OAuth 2.0 keys, there is no rotate option. Instead, you add a new key and switch to it before the old one expires.'

claims.claim: Auth scheme by service, as tagged in llms.txt: 73 services OAuth1.0a only, 7 OAuth1.0a and OAuth2 (FAPI 2.0), 5 MTLS, 5 NONE (documentation-only), 4 OpenBanking, out of 94 serviceId entries.
claims.quote: authType: OAuth1.0a and OAuth2 (FAPI 2.0)
claims.title: Mastercard Developers llms.txt
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Counts computed by grep of 'authType:' lines. MTLS services: Account to Account Commerce (CSP and DSP), Benefit Allocations Service (MTLS), Identity Insights for Accounts, Identity Insights for Transactions.

claims.claim: For mTLS APIs there are two named hosts: an MTF sandbox at mtf.services.mastercard.com and production at services.mastercard.com; client certificates can be issued in seconds on the portal from a portal-generated or custom CSR, or obtained from the Key Management Portal inside Mastercard Connect.
claims.quote: Sandbox mTLS certificates, which give access to an API sandbox that mimics a live Production environment (`mtf.services.mastercard.com`)
claims.title: Using mTLS to Access Mastercard APIs
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: 'Production MLTS certificates, which allow an application to access the Production environment (`services.mastercard.com`)'. 'The Key Management Portal (KMP) is an application available in Mastercard Connect' (link markup stripped). Uploading a certificate from an external CA is allowed 'ONLY ... if required by an API in your project'.

claims.claim: REST base URLs are published per API and follow one pattern: sandbox.api.mastercard.com/<service> for Sandbox and api.mastercard.com/<service> for Production.
claims.quote: Your client uses the Sandbox base URL: `https://sandbox.api.mastercard.com/bin-resources`.
claims.title: BIN Lookup - Testing
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Locations doc table lists 'Sandbox URL https://sandbox.api.mastercard.com/locations/atms' and 'Production URL https://api.mastercard.com/locations/atms'. Mastercom OpenAPI file lists server 'https://api.mastercard.com/mastercom' described as 'Global Production Server'. Errors doc uses 'openssl s_client -showcerts -host sandbox.api.mastercard.com -port 443'.

claims.claim: Sandbox data is mock, not published production data: BIN Lookup's sandbox returns randomly generated account ranges that are explicitly not real Mastercard BIN ranges.
claims.quote: The data in sandbox is entirely mocked information that uses realistic account ranges, but should not be used in any production system
claims.title: BIN Lookup - Testing
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Warning on the same page: 'The account ranges used in sandbox are randomly generated mocked data'. Sample BINs such as 99875393 are provided to trigger responses. Real BIN data (SBART file) requires sign-in per the BIN Lookup Support page.

claims.claim: Mastercom (disputes) is exposed on the developer portal as an OAuth 1.0a REST API with a sandbox that returns mocked responses and a public 308 KB OpenAPI 3.0.3 spec (mastercom-v6.yaml).
claims.quote: Try the application in our Sandbox environment and receive mocked responses.
claims.title: Mastercom
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Link markup stripped from quote. API Basics: 'Mastercard uses OAuth 1.0a for authenticating your application.' Spec https://static.developer.mastercard.com/content/mastercom/swagger/mastercom-v6.yaml fetched logged out (315,749 bytes, 'openapi: 3.0.3', contact apisupport@mastercard.com). A 2026-08-26 forum post asks how to obtain test claims/chargebacks in the Mastercom sandbox (1 reply).

claims.claim: A third, gated environment exists between Sandbox and Production for network-processing APIs: the Mastercard Test Facility (MTF), reached by emailing an assigned implementation manager rather than self-service.
claims.quote: Send an email to your assigned mastercard implementation manager with the sandbox key to request access to the MTF environment.
claims.title: MTF Access Guide
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: 'Your Mastercard implementation manager will create a test plan and test cases for testing in the MTF environment.' Mastercard Send release notes state each quarterly release is 'delivered to the Mastercard Test Facility (MTF) environment before Production'. The status page lists 'RPPS Biller Maintenance Service MTF' as a separate monitored service.

claims.claim: There is no portal-wide set of test cards; test PANs are product-specific and for some products a Mastercard representative must configure them.
claims.quote: Mastercard does not offer a generic set of test cards that can be used across products.
claims.title: Test Cards for Mastercard APIs
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Table links test cards for Loyalty Insurance, Mastercard Checkout Solutions (Click to Pay, Secure Card on File, MPQR SRC, Guest Checkout Tokenization, Virtual Card Tokens), Merchant Presented QR, and Mastercard Send. 'In some cases a Mastercard representative must work with customers directly to configure specific cards for testing.'

claims.claim: Mastercard Send publishes its test PANs openly, including test cards for competitor and ATM/debit networks (STAR, Pulse, NYCE, Visa OCT/AFT) alongside Mastercard, Maestro and MoneySend; MTF PAN spreadsheets are downloadable without login.
claims.quote: You can use any of these test PANs in your Sandbox API requests.
claims.title: Sandbox Test Cards
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Any future expiry (e.g. 2077-03) and any 3-digit CVC work. MTF page lists Test_Cards_US_MTF.xlsx 'updated 25 July 2022' and Test_Cards_MTF.xlsx 'updated 19 August 2026'; the latter fetched logged out (130,993 bytes). Pulse test PANs appear here despite Pulse now being Capital One-owned (acquisition closed 2025-05-18).

claims.claim: Official SDKs are thin auth/crypto libraries, not full API clients: oauth1-signer in Java, Node, Python, C#, Go, PHP, Ruby, Swift; client-encryption in Java, Node, Python, C#, Go, PHP, Ruby; oauth2-client in Java and JS; API clients are meant to be generated from OpenAPI specs. The GitHub org has 139 public repos.
claims.quote: Zero dependency library for generating a Mastercard API compliant OAuth signature.
claims.title: oauth1-signer-java README
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: GitHub REST API org record: 'public_repos': 139, is_verified true, created 2012-04-17. Latest releases (GitHub releases API): oauth1-signer-java v1.6.0 2026-03-05; -nodejs v1.2.0 2026-03-30; -python v1.9.2 2026-04-13; -csharp v1.5.1 2024-09-25; -go v1.2.5 2026-08-13; client-encryption-java v1.8.9 2026-08-12; -nodejs v1.10.8 2026-03-30; -python v1.23.3 2025-12-04; -csharp v1.9.4 2025-12-04; -go v1.4.0 2026-08-14; oauth2-client-java 1.0.3 2026-07-11; oauth2-client-js 1.0.0 2026-03-06. Registries: npm mastercard-oauth1-signer 1.2.0, mastercard-client-encryption 1.10.8; PyPI mastercard-oauth1-signer 1.9.2, mastercard-client-encryption 1.23.3; Maven repo1 com.mastercard.developer:oauth1-signer <latest>1.6.0</latest> (2026-03-05), client-encryption 1.8.9; NuGet Mastercard.Developer.ClientEncryption.Core 1.9.4. Signature methods: RSA_SHA256 default, RSA_PSS_SHA256 optional. Java libs require Java 17+ from 1.5.4.

claims.claim: The PHP, Ruby and Swift SDK repositories are archived on GitHub; oauth1-signer-php and client-encryption-php carry the 'deprecated-repository' topic, so those languages are no longer supported.
claims.quote: deprecated-repository
claims.title: oauth1-signer-php (GitHub repository metadata)
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Quote is a repository topic returned by the GitHub REST API (api.github.com/repos/Mastercard/oauth1-signer-php), which also returns archived: true. Also archived: client-encryption-php (topics include 'deprecated'), oauth1-signer-ruby, oauth1-signer-swift, sdk-core-php (last push 2020-09-16). Last releases: oauth1-signer-php v1.1.4 2022-05-05, -ruby v1.1.3 2023-09-06, -swift 1.1.0 2020-07-08.

claims.claim: Client-library deprecation policy: at least three months' notice via a GitHub 'maintenance | deprecated' label, then the repository is removed; supported runtimes are Java 17+, Node 19+, Python 3.9+, Go 1.20+, .NET Standard 2.1 and OpenAPI Generator 7.x.
claims.quote: The notice is issued at least three months before the end-of-life date.
claims.title: Mastercard Versioning and Deprecation Policy (CLIENT_LIBRARY_DEPRECATION_POLICY.md)
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: 'At the end of three months, we will remove the repository in which the depreciating version of the library resides.' Every SDK README links this policy. Fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com.

claims.claim: API (service) deprecation has no fixed notice period: the policy says services are rarely decommissioned and the timeline varies product by product, communicated to affected customers with contractual terms.
claims.quote: The timeline is often product and customer-impact dependent, so it varies from product to product.
claims.title: Mastercard Versioning and Deprecation Policy (CLIENT_LIBRARY_DEPRECATION_POLICY.md)
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Policy also warns that functionality 'may be changed without prior warning to patch a security vulnerability'. API versioning is per product (e.g. mastercom-v6, Account Validation spec versions 1.0.0 to 3.1.2); no portal-wide API versioning policy page was found.

claims.claim: There is no Mastercard-branded CLI; the recommended production path is to download the OpenAPI spec and generate a client with the third-party OpenAPI Generator CLI, then wire in Mastercard's signer and encryption libraries.
claims.quote: Download the OpenAPI Generator CLI (you can follow the instructions here)
claims.title: Generating and Configuring a Mastercard API Client
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Link markup stripped from quote. Tutorial covers Java, Python, NodeJS and C#. Quick Start calls this 'Option 3 ... (Best for Production-Ready Integrations)'. GitHub org search found no CLI repository; the closest developer tooling is the Insomnia plugin, Postman encryption lib and MCP server.

claims.claim: OpenAPI/Swagger specs are downloadable logged out as static YAML files from static.developer.mastercard.com; the spec is the unit of integration on the portal.
claims.quote: description: Global Production Server
claims.title: Mastercom Dispute Processing API (OpenAPI 3.0.3)
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Also fetched MDES_Digital_Enablement.yaml (91,934 bytes, 200). Quick Start: 'Download the API specification (OpenAPI or Swagger).' The per-service llms-full.txt front matter lists 'api_specification(s):' URLs, e.g. BIN-lookup-spec.yaml. Open Banking US spec is additionally maintained on GitHub (Mastercard/open-banking-us-openapi) with Swagger Editor and Redoc links.

claims.claim: Mastercard maintains an official public Postman workspace with forkable collections per API and three sandbox environments (plain, Mastercard encryption, JWE encryption); a 'Run in Postman' button sits on each API's docs.
claims.quote: Forking one of the collections hosted in the official Mastercard Postman workspace.
claims.title: Postman Collection
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Workspace https://www.postman.com/mastercard/workspace/mastercard-developers/overview resolved HTTP 200 logged out. Environments named 'Mastercard API Sandbox Environment', '... with Encryption', '... with JWE Encryption'. GitHub repos open-banking-us-postman and postman-encryption-lib (pre-request script for JWE/'mce' encryption) support this path.

claims.claim: An official Insomnia plugin (insomnia-plugin-mastercard, npm 2.7.1, 2026-07-08) signs requests with OAuth 1.0a or OAuth 2.0 and handles payload encryption and JWS signatures; one-click importable sandbox/production workspaces are published on GitHub.
claims.quote: It automatically computes and injects an `Authorization` header on outgoing requests, and can be configured to encrypt request payloads
claims.title: insomnia-plugin-mastercard README
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: npm registry: version 2.7.1 published 2026-07-08; GitHub release v2.7.1 2026-07-08. 'Compatibility: Insomnia v5.15.0+'. Developer Tools index names Postman and Insomnia as the 'Recommended path'.

claims.claim: Outbound notifications are called webhooks and are product-specific: Transaction Notifications requires an HTTPS endpoint with mutual TLS, immediate HTTP 200 acknowledgement, and retries failed deliveries for up to 24 hours before parking them for 7 days.
claims.quote: Mastercard marks the delivery as failed and retries at progressive intervals for up to 24 hours.
claims.title: Set Up Your Webhook (Transaction Notifications)
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: 'Your endpoint supports mutual TLS (MTLS) authentication.' Webhook URLs are 'Register[ed] ... during onboarding', not self-service in the portal. Ethoca Alerts for Merchants likewise exposes a 'Push API (Webhook)' requiring 'MSSL (mutual SSL/TLS authentication)' and the DigiCert Assured ID Root G2 trust anchor. Commercial Event Notifications and Account-to-Account Commerce also document 'Webhook Notifications'.

claims.claim: Open Finance US is consolidating its webhooks into a named subsystem, the Open Banking Webhook Management System (OBWMS), with existing services migrating during 2026; partners must allow-list about 30 published Mastercard source IP ranges.
claims.quote: Existing services will be migrated to the Open Banking Webhook Management System during 2026.
claims.title: Webhook Notifications (Open Finance US)
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Webhook families: Data Connect, Data Connect Components, Report Webhooks, TxPUSH. Page recommends webhook.site or beeceptor for testing. Note the inbound-IP allow-list here contrasts with the platform-level 'Recommendation Against IP Allow-Listing' for outbound calls to api.mastercard.com.

claims.claim: Rate limiting is enforced at the gateway on three axes (per IP, per service, per client) returning HTTP 429 with ReasonCode RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, but the actual TPS ceilings are placeholders and never published.
claims.quote: You have exceeded your rate limit. Maximum allowed: <max_client_tps> TPS.
claims.title: OAuth 1.0a and mTLS Error Codes
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: IP limit: 'Maximum allowed: <max_ip_tps> TPS'; service limit: '<max_service_tps> TPS'. Errors are flagged 'Recoverable: true'. A gateway payload cap also exists: 'Payload too large. Limit: <max_payload_size> KB'. No Retry-After header is documented.

claims.claim: Per-client call quotas are keyed to the first 48 characters of the consumer key and surfaced live in x-quota-current / x-quota-max / x-quota-period response headers; exceeding a quota returns HTTP 403 rather than 429.
claims.quote: The quota period values can be `month`, `day`, `hour`, `minute` or `second`.
claims.title: OAuth 1.0a and mTLS Error Codes
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: 'Client quotas will limit the number of calls that can be made per some time period with a particular consumer key.' Quota values themselves are not published.

claims.claim: Sensitive fields are protected by an application-layer encryption scheme in addition to TLS: JWE compact serialization (RSA-OAEP, AES-CBC or AES-GCM) for field-level or whole-payload encryption, plus a legacy 'Mastercard encryption' format; open-source client-encryption libraries implement both.
claims.quote: Mastercard uses JWE compact serialization for the encryption of sensitive data and supports both field level encryption and entire payload encryption.
claims.title: Securing Sensitive Data Using Payload Encryption
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Link markup stripped from quote. Legacy scheme 'involves an initialization vector, an encrypted or wrapped key, an encrypted value, a public key fingerprint and a digest algorithm' with RSA-OAEP SHA256/SHA512. Encryption certificates are issued per project via Credential Management.

claims.claim: Change cadence is per product rather than portal-wide: Mastercard Send ships quarterly releases (26.2, 26.3, 26.4 scheduled) to MTF then Production, publishes release notes three months ahead, and freezes changes 23 Nov 2026 to 1 Jan 2027; other products keep a dated 'Release History' table.
claims.quote: The main Mastercard Send API releases are quarterly, with each release delivered to the Mastercard Test Facility (MTF) environment before Production.
claims.title: Release Notes and Dates (Mastercard Send)
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Schedule: 26.2 MTF 21 July 2026 / Prod 25 Aug 2026; 26.3 MTF 13 Oct 2026 / Prod 10 Nov 2026; 26.4 Jan/Feb 2027. Account Validation Release History lists 8 dated entries from 'October 2024 1.0.0 API service launched' to '24 August 2026 3.1.2'; its 23 Jan 2026 3.0.0 entry 'Updated the API specification server domains to the new RNTZ domains'. llms.txt shows 44 'release notes' mentions across products; no single platform changelog exists.

claims.claim: Logged out, the product catalogue shows 91 products with category counts (Payments 55, Data 27, Security 20, Loyalty 12, Open Finance 4, New & Experimental 2) and audience filters (Issuer 58, Other Developers 52, Merchant 42, Acquirer 38, Fintech 11, Loyalty Providers 3).
claims.quote: View All 91 Featured 40 Data 27 Loyalty 12 New & Experimental 2 Open Finance 4 Payments 55 Security 20
claims.title: Mastercard Developers - Products
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Rendered logged out in a browser tab; whitespace collapsed in quote. Counts differ from llms.txt (74 product entries, 94 serviceIds) and from the status page (~110 monitored services); see contradictions. Some catalogue entries (e.g. Agent Suite for Merchants, Dynamic Yield, Consumer Credit Analytics) show 'Overview' only with no Documentation link.

claims.claim: No API pricing is published; product pages defer pricing to the production-access request or an account manager, while sandbox access is free.
claims.quote: Pricing is determined when requesting production access.
claims.title: Mastercard Developers llms.txt (Locations Intelligence overview)
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: BIN Lookup Support: 'For pricing details, contact your assigned Account Manager'. Open Banking US GitHub README: 'A free Mastercard Developers account is required to obtain your Partner ID, Partner Secret and App Key' and tests run on the 'Test Drive plan'. Only 4 'pricing' mentions in the whole llms.txt.

claims.claim: Mastercard runs a public, unauthenticated remote MCP server (developer.mcp.mastercard.com) plus an npm-installable local server so AI coding agents can discover services, read docs and pull operation schemas; a Claude Desktop .dxt bundle is also offered.
claims.quote: Use the server url <https://developer.mcp.mastercard.com> and "no Authentication" if prompted.
claims.title: Mastercard Developers Agent Toolkit
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: npm @mastercard/developers-mcp 0.1.7 (2026-05-16) and @mastercard/developers-agent-toolkit 0.1.6 (2026-05-08); GitHub developers-agent-toolkit last push 2026-06-21, no tagged release. Tools include get-services-list, get-api-operation-details, get-oauth10a/oauth20-integration-guide. GET on developer.mcp.mastercard.com returned HTTP 405 (endpoint expects MCP POST). Portal nav has an 'AI' top-level item.

claims.claim: The portal-wide llms-full.txt advertised in the docs and linked in the site footer is behind login (HTTP 401 redirect to /devzone/api/user/login), whereas llms.txt and every per-service llms-full.txt are public.
claims.quote: "code":"DP10005","message":"Session expired."
claims.title: llms-full.txt (401 response body)
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: curl -L final URL: https://developer.mastercard.com/devzone/api/user/login?heracles_operation=AUTHORIZATION&heracles_result_code=11001&referral_path=%2Fllms-full.txt. By contrast /bin-lookup/documentation/llms-full.txt returned 200 (189,086 bytes) and /mastercom/documentation/llms-full.txt 200 (298,929 bytes). The 'Working with llms.txt' page says llms-full.txt is per service, so the root link may be a broken or gated aggregate; see contradictions.

claims.claim: Mastercard Engage is presented on the developer support page as a directory of approved implementation specialists, but developer.mastercard.com/engage returns HTTP 401 and redirects to the portal login, so the directory itself is gated.
claims.quote: Mastercard Engage offers a directory of approved specialists that can implement and build your next solution
claims.title: Support at Mastercard Developers
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Rendered logged out in a browser tab. curl of https://developer.mastercard.com/engage: HTTP 401, final URL /devzone/api/user/login?...referral_path=%2Fengage. Forum categories include 'Partner Programs'. www.mastercard.com/engage returned 403 (WAF) and engage.mastercard.com did not resolve.

claims.claim: Mastercard Connect, the client portal that the developer docs point to for the Key Management Portal and Support Case Management, is a hard login wall requiring a User ID plus password or RSA SecurID token.
claims.quote: Sign in User ID Password / RSA SecurID® token
claims.title: Mastercard Connect
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Rendered in a browser tab; whitespace collapsed. curl: HTTP 302 to /mccsignin/users/auth-actions?heracles_operation=AUTHORIZATION... then 401. Page tagline: 'Where you connect with Mastercard to grow your business'; offers 'Sign up' and 'Replace RSA SecurID token'. Wall only documented; no login attempted.

claims.claim: Portal administration is itself API-driven: a 'Mastercard Developers API' mirrors the dashboard for onboarding customers and managing keys and credentials, and appears as a monitored service on the status page.
claims.quote: Any task you perform on the Dashboard can also be done via the API, and changes are reflected in both.
claims.title: Platform Overview
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: 'Integrate with the Developers API to automate a number of operational tasks such as onboarding and managing customers, creating and managing keys/credentials.' No documentation path for this API was found in llms.txt; the status page lists 'Mastercard Developers API'. This mainly serves program managers and SSO enterprise customers.

claims.claim: Mastercard's FY2025 10-K describes Mastercard Developers as the single access point for customers and partners to find and integrate APIs across its services.
claims.quote: Our Mastercard Developers platform makes it easy for customers and partners to leverage our many digital assets and services.
claims.title: Mastercard Incorporated Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Continues: 'By providing a single access point with tools and capabilities to find APIs across a broad range of Mastercard services, we enable easy integration of our services into new and existing solutions.' Self-descriptive language in a filing; no metrics (developer counts, API volumes) disclosed. Filed after the 2025-05-18 Capital One/Discover close.

claims.claim: A public status page at /api-status shows per-service health for Sandbox and Production separately, refreshed about once a minute, across roughly 110 services including Mastercom, Mastercard Send, MDES, Processing and Gateway.
claims.quote: Mastercard Developers performs health checks approximately once per minute.
claims.title: API Status | Mastercard Developers
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Rendered logged out in a browser tab. States: Healthy, Partially Degraded, Unreachable, Not available; toggles 'Sandbox' and 'Production'; columns CURRENT / SERVICE NAME / LAST 24HR. Open Finance AU/US show 'Status of this API is available on the details page.' Footer link text 'Status' resolves to href="/api-status".

claims.claim: Direct support tickets require login ('Get Help' opens only after sign-in), while the developer forum is readable logged out with four public categories and regional filters.
claims.quote: If you’d like to contact our support team directly, please sign in to your account:
claims.title: Support at Mastercard Developers
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Forum https://forum.developer.mastercard.com/s/ (Salesforce Experience Cloud '/s/' path) rendered logged out with categories 'General Questions Technical API Questions Finding the Right API Partner Programs', an 'Ask a question' button and posts showing replies/views/upvotes. claims.claim: Forum evidence of sandbox friction: a September 2026 developer reports every request to the Open Finance US sandbox (api.finicity.com) blocked by an Incapsula WAF from non-US networks, with no reply after two weeks.
claims.quote: Is Open Finance US Sandbox access geo-restricted to require requests originate from the United States?
claims.title: Sandbox API blocked by Incapsula WAF (403) — geo-restriction to US-origin traffic? (Mastercard Developers Forum)
claims.label: Reported
claims.note: Post showed '0 replies 16 views' on 2026-09-25. Poster reports the portal 'Usage dashboard shows 0 hits across every endpoint', i.e. requests never reach the API layer. Practitioner claim, not confirmed by Mastercard.

claims.claim: Forum evidence that sandbox test data is not always self-service: a developer testing Mastercom Queue, Claim, Chargeback and Case Filing APIs asks how to get sample claims loaded into their sandbox tenant.
claims.quote: Could you please advise how we can obtain test data (claims, chargebacks, case filings) in Sandbox?
claims.title: Mastercom Sandbox - How can we obtain test claims and queue data for API testing? (Mastercard Developers Forum)
claims.label: Reported
claims.note: Post showed '1 replies 55 views'. Consistent with the Mastercom docs' 'receive mocked responses' model and the test-cards page's 'a Mastercard representative must work with customers directly'.

claims.claim: Forum evidence of approval-gated sandboxes: a developer with a correctly signed OAuth 1.0a request gets 403 from the Fraud and Loss Database sandbox because the API sits at 'SANDBOX Pending' in their project.
claims.quote: Also i could see Confirmed Fraud API as "SANDBOX Pending" , not sure what is required to move it forward
claims.title: Receiving 403 while consuming https://sandbox.api.mastercard.com/fld/confirmed-frauds/issuer-frauds (Mastercard Developers Forum)
claims.label: Reported
claims.note: Post showed '1 replies 48 views', filed under 'Technical API Questions / Mastercom'. Matches the Quick Start FAQ on 'Under Review' sandbox status. A 2026-09-17 post 'Steps for going Developer Portal Production release' asks for 'Required artifacts Approval workflow and SLA' for production publication.

claims.claim: Mastercard advises partners not to IP-allow-list or certificate-pin api.mastercard.com, citing dynamic public infrastructure, and to connect by DNS hostname only.
claims.quote: Mastercard does not recommend IP Allow-Listing given the dynamic nature of our public-facing internet infrastructure.
claims.title: Recommendation Against IP Allow-Listing
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: 'Certificate pinning is not a recommended approach and Mastercard discourages it.' Relevant to acquirer/processor network teams; the Errors doc's TLS-handshake section attributes many failures to corporate proxies stripping certificates.

claims.claim: Marketing framing of the sandbox is 'build in minutes'; the portal positions Sandbox as a discovery tool before any commercial onboarding.
claims.quote: Our Sandbox allows developers to quickly see how our APIs work and discover what's possible.
claims.title: Platform Overview
claims.label: Vendor
claims.note: Heading 'Build in minutes'. Self-description without external check; the forum posts above show approval and WAF gates that lengthen time-to-first-call for some APIs.

claims.claim: 'Merchant Cloud' exists on the developer portal only as a documentation-only entry (authType NONE) carrying agentic-commerce tutorials and a 'Developer Playbook for Agentic Commerce'; it exposes no API, sandbox or credentials of its own.
claims.quote: With Merchant Cloud, we’re powering tomorrow’s growth by connecting the dots today, bringing industry-leading commerce solutions onto a single, open platform.
claims.title: Merchant Cloud Tutorials and Guides
claims.label: Vendor
claims.note: llms.txt block: 'serviceId: merchant-cloud', 'authType: NONE'. Guides listed: 'How AI Agents Are Transforming Commerce', 'What Is Agentic Commerce?', 'The Rails for Agentic Commerce'. The catalogue separately lists 'Agent Suite for Merchants' (Overview only, no Documentation link) and 'Mastercard Cloud Commerce' (3 documentation sets), which are different products.
